# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel (dual-write/dual-run) throughout the migration. Users are migrated in batches, with the legacy system remaining fully operational as a fallback until well after the last user batch has been verified stable on the new system. Decommissioning of the old system is treated as a separate, later initiative and is explicitly excluded from the phases below.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users — ~800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end QA in staging (invoicing, payment capture, refunds, proration, tax calculation) with 100% parity against the legacy system on a replayed sample of 10,000 historical transactions, and rollback tooling to revert a migrated account to the legacy system has been tested successfully.

**Scope:** Internal accounts and opted-in low-risk external users (e.g., monthly self-serve plans, no active disputes, no complex enterprise contracts).

**Duration:** 1–2 weeks, with daily monitoring.

---

## Phase 2: Expanded Rollout (25% of users — ~10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 cohort has run for a minimum of 10 full billing cycles (or 14 calendar days, whichever is longer) with zero critical billing discrepancies, support ticket volume for billing issues at or below Phase 1's pre-migration baseline, and sign-off from Finance on reconciliation accuracy.

**Scope:** Broadened to include mid-complexity accounts (multiple payment methods, recurring subscriptions, standard discounts), still excluding highest-value enterprise contracts.

**Duration:** 2–3 weeks, with twice-weekly reconciliation review.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability / Final Batch (73% of users — remaining ~29,200 users, including remaining standard and enterprise accounts)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 cohort shows a sustained error rate below the halt threshold (see Metrics below) for 2 consecutive weeks, all Phase 1 and Phase 2 accounts remain reconciled with no open critical incidents, and enterprise accounts have completed contract-specific validation (custom pricing, invoicing terms, multi-entity billing) in a staging dry run.

**Scope:** All remaining users, migrated in sub-batches (e.g., 5–10 sub-waves of ~3,000–6,000 users) to preserve the ability to pause between sub-waves without re-entering earlier phases.

**Duration:** 4–6 weeks.

*Note: The old billing system remains active, in read-only/fallback mode, for a minimum 90-day post-migration observation window after Phase 3 completes. Any decision to disable or decommission the legacy system is handled in a separate, subsequent phase outside this rollout plan, gated on its own entry criteria (e.g., zero fallback invocations for 30 consecutive days).*

---

## Halt Metric

If, during any phase, the **billing discrepancy rate** (transactions where new-system-calculated amount differs from legacy-system-calculated amount by more than $0.01) **exceeds 0.5% of processed transactions in any rolling 24-hour window**, the rollout is halted immediately, no further accounts are migrated, and the phase-in-progress cohort is triaged before any resumption decision is made.

Additional guardrail metrics to monitor (not sole halt triggers but escalation triggers):
- Failed payment capture rate increase of more than 20% relative to legacy baseline.
- Billing-related support ticket volume more than 2x the pre-migration baseline for that user segment.

---

## Risks

RISK: Payment processor tokenization mismatch causes duplicate or failed charges during account migration | Run a dry-run token validation pass against the processor's sandbox for every account prior to migration and require a successful token re-link confirmation before cutover | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Dual-running systems produce divergent invoices for the same billing cycle, causing customer-facing billing confusion | Implement automated daily reconciliation jobs comparing outputs from both systems for all migrated accounts, with alerting on any variance above threshold | Billing Platform Team
RISK: Enterprise accounts with custom contract terms (custom pricing, multi-entity invoicing) are migrated before the new system fully supports their configuration | Gate enterprise account migration behind a dedicated contract-parity validation checklist and require Finance/Legal sign-off before inclusion in Phase 3 | Enterprise Accounts Manager
RISK: Rollback procedure fails or is too slow when a migrated account needs to revert to the legacy system, causing extended billing downtime for affected customers | Test and time the rollback procedure against a statistically significant sample before each phase, and require rollback execution under a defined SLA (e.g., under 1 hour) as an entry criterion for the next phase | Site Reliability Engineering Lead
RISK: Customer support staff are unfamiliar with the new system's billing workflows, leading to mishandled customer inquiries during migration | Deliver targeted support team training and updated runbooks before each phase begins, gated behind a training-completion checkpoint | Customer Support Operations Lead

PHASES: 3
